week.weeklyOverview: This week toddlers explore how apples become familiar kitchen foods through smell, touch, mash, pour, and pretend cooking—never knives or stoves. They play as little apple chefs: mash soft cooked apple pieces, stir pretend applesauce, pour and measure with large cups, and run a simple Apple Juice Café and pie bakery. The week stays short-turn, sensory, and play-based with allergy-aware tasting that is always optional. Expect parallel play, brief attention bursts, and lots of repetition with the same kitchen props.
week.objectives:
Social-emotional: Practice turn-taking at kitchen centers and try new smells/tastes without pressure.
Language: Hear and try kitchen words such as mix, stir, measure, pour, mash, chef, and recipe.
Cognitive: Notice before/after apple changes and follow simple 2–3 step pretend recipes.
Fine motor: Scoop, pour, stir, stamp, and collage with large toddler tools.
Gross motor: March, dance, and carry props during bakery and chef parades.
Sensory: Explore apple smell/taste (optional), wet/dry mash play, and dough textures.
Creative: Make process chef hats, jar crafts, cartons, and open-ended recipe books.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Everyday: play kitchen, bowls, large measuring cups/spoons, wooden spoons, muffin tins, pie pans, aprons, baskets, smocks, towels, trays
Food (allergy-aware, optional tasting): whole apples for looking, pre-cooked cooled soft apple pieces, store-bought applesauce, apple juice for smelling/pouring demos
Art: washable paint, paper, glue sticks, pre-cut shapes, stickers, recycled clean jars/cartons, dot markers
Sensory: soft cooked apple pieces, potato mashers, play dough “pie dough,” shallow tubs
Dramatic play: chef hats, café cups, menus with pictures, trays
Literacy: Ten Red Apples; Apple Farmer Annie; Apple Pie ABC; The Apple Pie Tree
Optional printables: picture recipe cards; café/bakery zone signs
week.teacherPreparation:
Before Monday: allergy survey for apple/cinnamon; decide tasting vs smell-only plan.
Cook and fully cool soft apple pieces for mash/taste stations (teacher-only knife/stove work).
Sanitize play kitchen tools; remove tiny utensils.
Pre-cut hat bands, jar labels, carton shapes, and recipe-book pages.
Stage reusable kitchen zones (Wash / Mix / Serve) that can stay all week.
Choose 2–3 apple books for the reading basket.
prepChecklist: Complete apple allergy check with families
Teacher-cook and cool soft apple pieces (no child knives/stoves)
Sanitize bowls, mashers, cups, and play kitchen
Pre-cut craft shapes and hat bands
week.observationFocus:
Willingness to smell/taste with choice
Kitchen vocabulary attempts
Turn-taking at popular centers
Pouring/stirring control
Sensory preferences during mash/dough play
Engagement in pretend chef roles
week.familyConnection: Invite families to notice an apple food at home (sauce, juice, pie, or fresh apple) and name one kitchen action together—wash, stir, or pour. Optional: share a favorite family apple recipe photo—no required homework. Remind families tasting at school is always optional.
week.adaptations: Offer watching-first entry, smell-only alternatives to tasting, larger handles, picture recipe cards, and shorter turns. Never force tasting. Provide dry mash alternatives for children who dislike wet textures.

activities.title: Make Homemade Applesauce
activities.objective: Explore how soft cooked apples become applesauce through smell, optional taste, and supervised mashing—without knives or stoves.
activities.description: Teacher provides fully cooled soft apple pieces. Toddlers smell, look, and may mash with a potato masher or wooden spoon. Optional tiny tastes of cooled applesauce or mash; never forced. Pretend cooking is equally valued.
activities.materials:
Pre-cooked, fully cooled soft apple pieces (teacher-prepared)
Potato mashers or sturdy wooden spoons
Bowls and trays
Optional: store-bought cooled applesauce for tasting cups
Smocks; wipes; handwashing station
Picture card: apple → mash → sauce
activities.preparation: Allergy check. Cook/cool apples before children arrive. Portion small amounts. Set smell-only cups for children who decline tasting.
activities.setup: Low table with smocks, one bowl per 1–2 children, mashers, and a clear “cool food only” cue card.
activities.steps:
1. Wash hands together.
2. Show whole apple, then cooled soft pieces—name smell and soft.
3. Model one gentle mash; invite toddlers to mash.
4. Offer optional smell or tiny taste; accept “no thank you.”
5. Narrate change: chunky → mashy → sauce-like.
6. All done: wipe hands and rest tools.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Smell the apple—mm, sweet!
Can you mash, mash?
Is it soft or hard?
Would you like a tiny taste, or just smell?
No thank you is okay.
We made applesauce together!
activities.observationOpportunities: Approach/avoidance to food textures, willingness to mash, language for soft/mash/sauce, and comfort declining taste.
activities.safetyNotes: NO child knives, peelers, or stove use. Food must be fully cool. Allergy awareness. Supervise mashers. Never force tasting. Sanitize after mouthing.
activities.cleanupTips: Compost scraps if allowed; wash bowls/mashers; wipe table; change smocks.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Mash at an outdoor sensory table with the same cooled pieces.
teacherTips: Keep portions tiny to reduce waste and overwhelm.
Celebrate pretend stirring as success equal to tasting.

substitutions.use: Store-bought applesauce to stir (cool) or brown play-dough “apples” for full pretend

activities.adaptations: Offer spoon-stir only; provide dry oatmeal “pretend sauce” for texture-sensitive children; allow watching first.
activities.extensions: Compare chunky vs smooth samples side by side (smell/look).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers mash; younger hold a spoon and feel steam-free warm (not hot) bowls if used—prefer fully cool.
observationPrompts: Did the child mash with intent?
Did they use a food word?
How did they respond to optional tasting?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Realistic daycare table with cooled soft apple pieces in bowls, toddler-sized potato mashers, smocks, and a teacher nearby. No knives or stove. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Chef Hat Decorating
activities.objective: Create process-art chef hats that toddlers can wear during kitchen play, focusing on sticking and stamping—not a perfect product.
activities.description: Toddlers decorate pre-formed paper chef hats or bands with stickers, stamps, and large crayon marks. Process art only; no template matching.
activities.materials:
Pre-formed paper chef hats or sturdy paper bands
Large apple stickers
Washable stampers
Crayons/dot markers
Glue sticks
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-size hats/bands for toddler heads. Portion stickers. Remove tiny embellishments.
activities.setup: Art tray with one hat per child and limited open-ended materials.
activities.steps:
1. Try on a plain hat and name “chef.”
2. Invite sticking, stamping, and marking anywhere.
3. Narrate choices without correcting placement.
4. Help tape/fit hats loosely.
5. Wear hats to the play kitchen.
activities.teacherLanguage:
You are a kitchen chef!
Where will your sticker go?
Stamp, stamp.
Your hat is ready for cooking.
activities.observationOpportunities: Fine-motor sticking, creative choices, interest in role dress-up.
activities.safetyNotes: Large stickers only. Supervise glue. Hats should not cover eyes; no strings that cinch tightly.
activities.cleanupTips: Cap markers; save unused stickers; store hats on named hooks if reusing same day.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Decorate on a shaded picnic table.
teacherTips: Offer blank hats for children who prefer less decoration.
Replace activity framing: process identity play, not craft perfection.

substitutions.use: Paper plate bands or tea towels as aprons

activities.adaptations: Pre-stick one starter sticker; hand-under-hand support; allow apron-only option.
activities.extensions: Add a picture name card on the band.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants decorate a paper plate “hat” on the table without wearing.
observationPrompts: Did the child choose materials independently?
Did wearing the hat spark kitchen play?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Process-art table with paper chef hats, large stickers, and stampers—no sample-to-copy. Realistic daycare. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com
activities.decisionNote: Replace thin craft product focus with process-art chef identity play

activities.title: Measure the Ingredients
activities.objective: Practice filling and dumping large measuring cups with safe dry fillers to build early measure/pour vocabulary.
activities.description: Toddlers scoop dry oats, rice, or crumpled paper “ingredients” into large cups and bowls, hearing words full, empty, more, and all done.
activities.materials:
Large measuring cups and spoons
Bowls
Dry oats OR rice OR crumpled paper
Tray with sides
Smocks
Picture cards: full / empty
activities.preparation: Allergy check for oats. Choose paper filler if mouthing is heavy. Pre-portion filler.
activities.setup: Tray table for 2–3 toddlers with cups and one shared filler bin.
activities.steps:
1. Show empty cup and full cup.
2. Scoop together—count playfully “one scoop” without drills.
3. Pour into a bowl.
4. Notice full/empty.
5. Dump and repeat.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Is it full or empty?
Scoop, scoop.
Pour carefully.
More or all done?
activities.observationOpportunities: Scoop control, bilateral pouring attempts, vocabulary echoes for full/empty.
activities.safetyNotes: Supervise dry goods for mouthing. No small measuring spoons that are choking hazards. Allergy awareness.
activities.cleanupTips: Sweep filler; wash cups; recycle paper.
activities.indoorAlternatives: Use paper filler for easiest cleanup.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Water measuring with large cups outdoors (weather permitting).
teacherTips: Keep math playful—no accurate measuring expectations.

substitutions.use: Torn paper, cotton balls, or water play outdoors

activities.adaptations: Larger scoops; pre-filled cups to dump only; seated pouring over a tub.
activities.extensions: Match cup size: big cup / little cup.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger dump; older scoop and pour.
observationPrompts: Did the child attempt pour?
Did they respond to full/empty?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler measuring station with large cups, bowls, and dry filler on a tray. Realistic. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Little Apple Kitchen
activities.objective: Engage in toddler kitchen dramatic play with a few clear apple-cooking props and short role turns.
activities.description: Toddlers wash pretend apples, stir bowls, serve on plates, and take turns as chef and customer in a simple play kitchen.
activities.materials:
Play kitchen or low table
Toy/plastic apples or red pom stand-ins (large)
Bowls, spoons, plates
Aprons/chef hats
Dish tub with damp cloth “wash”
Picture menu: sauce / juice / pie
activities.preparation: Limit props to 6–8 items. Stage Wash / Mix / Serve signs. Sanitize toys.
activities.setup: Three clear zones: Wash, Mix, Serve. Keep walkways clear.
activities.steps:
1. Tour the three zones.
2. Model: wash apple → stir bowl → serve plate.
3. Invite 2–3 toddlers to play.
4. Narrate chef language; rotate roles.
5. Close kitchen: wash tools and rest.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Who is the chef today?
Wash the apple.
Stir, stir.
Order please—applesauce?
Thank you, chef!
activities.observationOpportunities: Role-taking, sequencing 2–3 steps, peer turn-taking, kitchen vocabulary.
activities.safetyNotes: Large props only. Damp cloth wash—not standing water if splash risk. No real knives.
activities.cleanupTips: Sort props into zone bins; wipe surfaces.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Blanket picnic kitchen outdoors with the same three zones.
teacherTips: Less is best for younger toddlers.
Join briefly as customer, then step back.

substitutions.use: Low table + dish tub + basket of bowls

activities.adaptations: One-step jobs (“put apple in bowl”). Picture sequence cards. Parallel play welcome.
activities.extensions: Add a waiting stool for “customers.”
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Preschoolers can take orders; toddlers stay on wash/stir.
observationPrompts: Did the child attempt more than one kitchen step?
Did they use chef/cook words?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Realistic toddler dramatic-play kitchen with plastic apples, bowls, aprons, and Wash/Mix/Serve zones. Cover candidate. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Mash the Apples
activities.objective: Build arm strength and sensory curiosity by mashing soft cooled apple pieces with large tools.
activities.description: Focused mash invitation: toddlers press and mash cooled soft apples (or applesauce) in sturdy bowls, noticing sound and texture.
activities.materials:
Cooled soft apple pieces or thick applesauce
Potato mashers / thick spoons
Bowls; trays; smocks
Optional cinnamon smell jar (closed) for sniffing only
activities.preparation: Allergy check including cinnamon if used for smell. Cool food fully. Set smell-only option.
activities.setup: Standing or seated mash station for 2 toddlers at a time.
activities.steps:
1. Hands washed.
2. Listen to mash sounds together.
3. Mash freely.
4. Optional smell of cinnamon jar.
5. Optional taste; accept declines.
6. Clean hands.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Mash, mash—what do you hear?
Squishy or smooth?
Your arms are working hard!
All done mashing?
activities.observationOpportunities: Persistence, sensory tolerance, grip strength, word attempts for soft/squish.
activities.safetyNotes: Fully cool. No knives. Allergy awareness. Never force tasting. Supervise tools.
activities.cleanupTips: Wash tools immediately; wipe sticky floors.
teacherTips: If children tire, switch to spoon stir.

substitutions.use: Yellow play dough balls to smash

activities.adaptations: Hand-over-hand mash; dry beanbag “apples” to press for non-food version.
activities.extensions: Compare mashed vs unmashed piece (look only).
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger poke with spoon; older mash with masher.
observationPrompts: How long did they persist?
Any texture refusal cues?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Close-up realistic mash station with potato masher in a bowl of soft apple pieces. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Before and After Apples
activities.objective: Notice simple before/after changes using whole apples, soft cooked pieces, and applesauce as look/smell samples.
activities.description: Toddlers explore three samples—whole apple, soft cooked piece, and applesauce—pointing to which changed and describing with teacher language.
activities.materials:
Whole apple
Cooled cooked apple piece
Applesauce in clear cup
Tray; magnifying glasses (optional)
Before/After picture cards
activities.preparation: Prep samples (teacher-cooked). Label trays with picture icons.
activities.setup: Small group at a discovery tray; samples behind a look-first boundary if needed.
activities.steps:
1. Show whole apple—hard, round.
2. Show cooked piece—soft.
3. Show sauce—mashy.
4. Invite pointing: before/after.
5. Optional smell; optional taste of sauce only.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What changed?
Hard or soft?
Which one is applesauce?
Before… after!
activities.observationOpportunities: Attention to differences, pointing, vocabulary for hard/soft/change.
activities.safetyNotes: Allergy check. Cool foods. No hot items. Optional tasting only.
activities.cleanupTips: Discard tasted samples; sanitize tray.

substitutions.use: Photos of before/after plus applesauce to smell

activities.adaptations: Two samples only; hand-over-hand pointing; watching allowed.
activities.extensions: Add juice cup as another “after” food made from apples.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older toddlers sort cards; younger match objects to pictures.
observationPrompts: Did the child point to a difference?
Did they echo hard/soft?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Discovery tray with whole apple, soft cooked piece, and applesauce cup labeled before/after. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Applesauce Jar Craft
activities.objective: Make an open-ended process collage on a jar shape or clean recycled jar—process art, not a look-alike product.
activities.description: Toddlers glue tissue, paper scraps, and stickers onto jar cutouts or clean plastic jars to make “applesauce jars” their own way.
activities.materials:
Jar-shaped paper OR clean plastic jars
Tissue paper scraps
Glue sticks
Apple stickers
Brown crayon for “lid” marks
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-cut jar shapes. Remove glass—use plastic only. Portion glue.
activities.setup: Art table with limited collage materials.
activities.steps:
1. Show a jar shape—say “applesauce jar.”
2. Glue and stick freely.
3. Optional scribble lid.
4. Display at child height.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What color goes on your jar?
Sticky glue.
Your jar is unique!
Applesauce ready?
activities.observationOpportunities: Glue control, material choices, pride in display.
activities.safetyNotes: Plastic jars only (no glass). Large scraps. Supervise glue caps.
activities.cleanupTips: Close glue; dry flat; recycle scraps.

substitutions.use: Paper cups to collage as jars

activities.adaptations: Pre-glue dots; sticker-only option; seated with tray boundaries.
activities.extensions: Fill jar picture with torn brown paper “sauce.”
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger stickers only; older add torn paper layers.
observationPrompts: Did the child engage with glue or stickers?
Did they name jar/sauce?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Process collage jars with tissue and stickers—no identical samples. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Stir the Applesauce
activities.objective: Move arms and bodies to a stirring chant, connecting music with kitchen actions.
activities.description: Toddlers pretend to stir giant invisible (or bowl) applesauce to a simple chant, changing slow/fast and freeze.
activities.materials:
Optional empty bowls and spoons
Music player (soft)
Open floor space
LLH Stir the Applesauce Chant
activities.preparation: Clear space. Practice slow/fast cues.
activities.setup: Circle or scattered standing spots with room to stir arms.
activities.steps:
1. Show stirring motion.
2. Chant and stir slowly.
3. Stir fast—then freeze.
4. Stir low / stir high.
5. Sit and rest spoons.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Stir, stir, round and round.
Slow… fast!
Freeze—hot sauce cooling!
One more stir!
activities.observationOpportunities: Imitation, speed changes, stopping on freeze, joy in group rhythm.
activities.safetyNotes: Space children out. No running with spoons. Soft volume.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect bowls/spoons.
teacherTips: Offer seated stirring for balance needs.

substitutions.use: Hands only stirring motions

activities.adaptations: Hand-over-hand stir; scarves as stir ribbons.
activities.extensions: Let a child be the “chef” who says slow/fast.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants bounce on laps with stir motions; toddlers stand.
observationPrompts: Did the child match slow/fast?
Could they freeze?

activities.title: Apple Juice Investigation
activities.objective: Investigate apple juice with look/smell/optional sip, noticing color and wetness compared with water.
activities.description: Toddlers explore small cups of water and apple juice: look through, smell, tip gently, and talk about same/different. Tasting is optional.
activities.materials:
Clear cups
Water
Apple juice (allergy-aware)
Trays; paper towels
Picture cards: water / juice
Smocks
activities.preparation: Allergy check. Pour tiny amounts. Plan smell-only cups.
activities.setup: Discovery table with paired cups for 2–3 children.
activities.steps:
1. Wash hands.
2. Look: which is yellow/brown?
3. Smell each.
4. Optional tiny sip; accept no.
5. Tip on tray to see wet (teacher-controlled pour demo if needed).
6. Wipe and done.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What color do you see?
Smell—sweet juice?
Same or different?
Sip or no thank you?
activities.observationOpportunities: Sensory curiosity, comparison language, comfort with choice.
activities.safetyNotes: Allergy awareness. Tiny amounts. No choking gulps—slow sips. Wipe spills to prevent slips.
activities.cleanupTips: Wash cups; sanitize table; mop spills.
activities.outdoorAlternatives: Investigate at water table with juice smell jar + water play separated.
teacherTips: Separate tasting cups from exploration cups.

substitutions.use: Apple juice concentrate smell on cotton in a jar + water look cups

activities.adaptations: Smell-only pathway; sealed look bottles; watching first.
activities.extensions: Add applesauce cup as a third “apple food.”
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger look/smell; older help pour with two hands into a tub.
observationPrompts: Did the child compare the two liquids?
Did they exercise a tasting choice?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Clear cups of water and apple juice on a toddler tray for look/smell investigation. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pour and Measure
activities.objective: Practice two-handed pouring between large cups to build coordination and kitchen measure words.
activities.description: Toddlers pour water or dry filler from pitcher to cup using large tools over a tub, hearing pour, careful, full, and stop.
activities.materials:
Large plastic pitchers
Large cups
Shallow tub
Water OR dry filler
Smocks; towels
Funnel (optional large)
activities.preparation: Fill pitchers halfway. Set towels. Choose water day or dry day.
activities.setup: Pouring station over a tub for 2 children.
activities.steps:
1. Model two hands on pitcher.
2. Pour to a line or until “stop.”
3. Child pours.
4. Switch pourer/helper.
5. Squeeze towels—all done.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Two hands.
Pour carefully.
Stop!
Full cup.
You did it!
activities.observationOpportunities: Two-hand control, stopping response, frustration tolerance with spills.
activities.safetyNotes: Wipe spills. No glass. Supervise to prevent drinking non-potable water if reused; use clean water for tasting-free play.
activities.cleanupTips: Dump water; dry floor; wash tools.

substitutions.use: Large cups pouring into bowls

activities.adaptations: Teacher holds pitcher while child tips; use squeeze bottles for easier control.
activities.extensions: Pour to fill two cups for a café order.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger dump cups; older use pitcher.
observationPrompts: Did they try two hands?
Did they stop when asked?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler pouring station with large pitcher, cups, and tub. Realistic daycare. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Apple Juice Carton Craft
activities.objective: Transform a clean recycled carton or carton shape into process-art “apple juice” packaging.
activities.description: Toddlers paint, sticker, and collage clean empty juice cartons or cardboard carton cutouts. Process art only.
activities.materials:
Clean empty juice cartons OR cardboard carton shapes
Washable paint + large brushes
Stickers; glue; paper scraps
Smocks; newspaper
activities.preparation: Rinse cartons; tape sharp edges. Pre-cut shapes if not using cartons.
activities.setup: Painting/collage table with one carton per child.
activities.steps:
1. Name “juice carton.”
2. Paint or collage freely.
3. Add stickers if desired.
4. Dry on rack.
5. Use later in café play.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What color is your juice carton?
Brush up and down.
Sticky sticker!
Your juice for the café!
activities.observationOpportunities: Brush grip, covering choices, connection to dramatic play props.
activities.safetyNotes: Clean food-safe exterior only; no drinking from craft cartons. Supervise paint.
activities.cleanupTips: Dry cartons; wash brushes; trash liners.
teacherTips: Plan café reuse the same afternoon.

substitutions.use: Paper bags taped as cartons

activities.adaptations: Sticker-only; sponge stamps; seated with tray.
activities.extensions: Add a picture “apple” label children choose.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger stickers; older paint broader surfaces.
observationPrompts: Did the child engage in process covering?
Did they bring carton to café later?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Process-painted juice cartons drying on a rack in a classroom. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Apple Juice Café
activities.objective: Practice simple café roles—customer and server—with picture menus and pretend or optional real juice service.
activities.description: Toddlers run a tiny Apple Juice Café: point to a menu picture, “pour” pretend juice, serve on a tray, and say please/thank you.
activities.materials:
Low table café
Picture menus (juice / sauce / water)
Cups; trays
Carton props from craft
Chairs; apron
Optional: tiny cooled juice tasting cups (allergy-aware)
activities.preparation: Allergy plan. Limit to 2 seats. Stage menu photos large.
activities.setup: Counter + 2 customer seats. Server apron ready.
activities.steps:
1. Open café—show menu pictures.
2. Customer points to order.
3. Server pours pretend juice.
4. Optional real tiny taste in separate cups.
5. Thank you; rotate roles.
6. Closed sign—clean up.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Welcome to the café!
What would you like?
Pour, pour.
Here’s your juice.
Thank you!
activities.observationOpportunities: Role exchange, pointing communication, courtesy words, pouring in context.
activities.safetyNotes: Allergy awareness. Separate pretend cups from tasting cups. Wipe spills.
activities.cleanupTips: Wash tasting cups; sort props; wipe table.
teacherTips: Keep café open in short bursts.

substitutions.use: Paper plates as servers

activities.adaptations: Teacher as co-server; nonverbal pointing only; one-role day.
activities.extensions: Add a “to-go” basket.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Older take orders with clipboard pictures; toddlers serve/pour.
observationPrompts: Did the child take both roles over time?
Did they use please/thank you with support?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler café table with picture menus, cups, trays, and carton props. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Pretend Apple Pie Bakers
activities.objective: Explore pretend pie baking with pie pans, dough, and apple fillers using safe toddler tools only.
activities.description: Toddlers press play-dough crusts into pans, add red pom or paper apple pieces, and “bake” in a play oven or box oven—no real heat.
activities.materials:
Pie pans
Play dough
Large red poms or paper apple shapes
Play oven or cardboard box oven
Aprons; rolling pins (large)
Picture recipe: press → fill → bake
activities.preparation: Soften dough. Remove tiny cutters. Check pom size (too large to choke).
activities.setup: Bakery tray for 2–3 bakers.
activities.steps:
1. Press dough in pan.
2. Add apple fillers.
3. Carry to pretend oven.
4. Ding—cool pie!
5. Serve pretend slices.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Press the crust.
Apples in the pie.
Into the oven!
Ding—careful, cooling.
Want a pretend slice?
activities.observationOpportunities: Sequencing with pictures, pretend oven use, peer sharing of pans.
activities.safetyNotes: No real oven/heat. Large poms only. Supervise dough mouthing.
activities.cleanupTips: Store dough; sort fillers; wipe pans.

substitutions.use: Damp sand crusts outdoors or flattened brown clay

activities.adaptations: Pre-pressed crusts; fill-only job; watching bakers.
activities.extensions: Add cinnamon smell jar to “season” pies.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger fill pans; older roll dough.
observationPrompts: Did the child follow 2+ recipe steps?
Did they use bake/pie words?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler bakery tray with pie pans, dough, and apple fillers beside a play oven. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Apple Pie Dough
activities.objective: Explore soft dough textures through squish, pat, and roll with large tools.
activities.description: Open sensory dough play themed as pie dough—toddlers squash, poke, and roll without a required product.
activities.materials:
Soft play dough or safe salt dough
Large rolling pins
Pie pans
Smocks; wipes
Optional: safe apple scent (very light) mixed by teacher
activities.preparation: Allergy check for wheat if using flour dough; offer gluten-free dough alternative. Soften dough.
activities.setup: Sensory table or trays for 3 children.
activities.steps:
1. Offer dough—feel soft.
2. Squish and poke.
3. Roll if interested.
4. Optional press into pan.
5. Store dough balls for next time.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Soft dough.
Squish!
Roll, roll.
Pat, pat.
How does it feel?
activities.observationOpportunities: Texture tolerance, tool use, calming sensory engagement.
activities.safetyNotes: Supervise mouthing; replace dough if mouthed heavily. Allergy awareness for flour.
activities.cleanupTips: Wipe table; store dough sealed; wash hands.

substitutions.use: Cloud dough or soft kinetic sand if safe for age

activities.adaptations: Tools only for touch-sensitive children; smaller dough ball; seated support.
activities.extensions: Hide a large pom “apple” in dough to find.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants explore a sealed dough bag; toddlers open play.
observationPrompts: Did they tolerate dough touch?
Did they use a tool?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Sensory trays with soft dough, rolling pins, and pie pans. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Measure the Pie Ingredients
activities.objective: Scoop and dump pretend pie ingredients with large cups while hearing measure words in a bakery context.
activities.description: Toddlers measure “flour,” “apples,” and “sugar” using large cups into a mixing bowl—playful dumping, not accurate recipes.
activities.materials:
Large measuring cups
Mixing bowl
White paper scrap “flour”
Red paper/pom “apples”
Optional oats “sugar” (allergy check)
Spoons; tray
activities.preparation: Portion fillers in separate bins with picture labels.
activities.setup: Bakery measure station for 2 toddlers.
activities.steps:
1. Point to ingredient pictures.
2. Scoop one ingredient.
3. Dump into bowl.
4. Stir pretend batter/pie mix.
5. All done—dump back to bins.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What do we need for pie?
One scoop of flour.
Apples in!
Mix, mix.
All done measuring.
activities.observationOpportunities: Picture matching, scooping, simple choice-making.
activities.safetyNotes: Allergy check. Large pieces only. Supervise mouthing of oats.
activities.cleanupTips: Sort fillers back; wipe bowl.
teacherTips: Keep counts playful (“one scoop”), not skill drills.
Picture labels matter more than numbers.

substitutions.use: Single filler + picture cards naming pretend ingredients

activities.adaptations: One ingredient only; teacher scoops while child dumps.
activities.extensions: Carry measured bowl to pretend oven.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger dump; older choose ingredients by picture.
observationPrompts: Did the child scoop and dump?
Did they reference a picture ingredient?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Measuring cups and ingredient bins labeled with pictures for pie play. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Bakery Dance Party
activities.objective: Celebrate bakery play with joyful movement—knead, sprinkle, and march to music.
activities.description: Toddlers dance bakery actions: knead feet/hands, sprinkle arms, and march like delivering pies, freezing when the music pauses.
activities.materials:
Open space
Music player
Optional scarves
Picture action cards: knead / sprinkle / march
activities.preparation: Clear path. Choose 2–3 short tracks or chant.
activities.setup: Scatter spots; show action cards.
activities.steps:
1. Knead the dough—push arms.
2. Sprinkle sugar—fingers flutter.
3. March deliver pies.
4. Freeze—pies cooling.
5. Bow to customers—done.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Knead, knead!
Sprinkle!
March, march—pies ready!
Freeze!
Hooray bakers!
activities.observationOpportunities: Imitation, rhythm, stop/start listening, group joy.
activities.safetyNotes: No running. Soft landings. Clear toys from floor.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect scarves/cards.

substitutions.use: Teacher clap/chant only

activities.adaptations: Hand-holding march; scarf only for children who avoid stomping.
activities.extensions: Child chooses next bakery action card.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants bounce; toddlers dance.
observationPrompts: Did the child try two actions?
Did they freeze?

activities.title: Apple Recipe Review
activities.objective: Review the week’s apple foods with pictures and props, inviting toddlers to choose favorites and retell simple kitchen actions.
activities.description: Toddlers visit a review tray with pictures/props for applesauce, juice, and pie, acting out wash/mash/pour/bake briefly.
activities.materials:
Picture cards: sauce, juice, pie
Related props (masher, cup, pie pan)
Basket
Optional favorite tasting (allergy-aware, optional)
activities.preparation: Gather week props. Plan optional tasting cups.
activities.setup: Circle or small-group review rug.
activities.steps:
1. Show three apple foods.
2. Children choose a favorite picture.
3. Act the matching action briefly.
4. Optional smell/taste.
5. Cheer: “Apple chefs!”
activities.teacherLanguage:
Which apple food do you like?
Mash for sauce?
Pour for juice?
Bake for pie?
You remember!
activities.observationOpportunities: Recall of week experiences, preference expression, action imitation.
activities.safetyNotes: Optional tasting only; allergy check. Keep review short.
activities.cleanupTips: Return props to theme basket.
teacherTips: Accept pointing as a full answer.

substitutions.use: Real empty sauce jar, juice carton, pie pan as cues

activities.adaptations: Two choices only; adult narrates child’s action.
activities.extensions: Family note with three pictures to talk about at home.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger hold prop; older tell a two-word retell.
observationPrompts: Did the child indicate a favorite?
Did they attempt a related action?

activities.title: My Favorite Apple Recipe Book
activities.objective: Assemble a simple process-art “recipe book” with stickers and marks—no writing required.
activities.description: Toddlers make 2–3 page paper books: glue apple pictures, stick stickers, and scribble as their recipe marks.
activities.materials:
Pre-stapled 3-page booklets
Apple magazine cutouts or pre-cut apples
Glue sticks; stickers; crayons
Smocks
activities.preparation: Pre-make blank booklets. Pre-cut large images. Write child’s name if desired.
activities.setup: Art table with booklets and open-ended collage materials.
activities.steps:
1. Show a blank book—“my recipes.”
2. Glue/stick on pages freely.
3. Scribble recipe marks.
4. “Read” book to a friend or stuffed animal.
5. Take home or display.
activities.teacherLanguage:
What’s on this page?
Sticky apple.
Your marks are your recipe!
Can you show your book?
activities.observationOpportunities: Page turning, collage engagement, emergent “reading” pretend.
activities.safetyNotes: Large cutouts. Supervise staples on finished books (pre-stapled by teacher).
activities.cleanupTips: Dry pages; stack books with names visible.

substitutions.use: Single folded paper card

activities.adaptations: Sticker-only book; adult turns pages while child sticks.
activities.extensions: Add a photo of the child as chef on the cover.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger one-page placemat; older three-page book.
observationPrompts: Did the child engage across pages?
Did they pretend to read?
activities.imageBriefSetup: Toddler process-art recipe booklets with apple stickers and scribbles. Footer: littlelearnershubbyleah.com

activities.title: Kitchen Measuring Relay
activities.objective: Carry and deliver measuring cups along a short path to build gross-motor control and kitchen teamwork.
activities.description: Toddlers walk a short relay path carrying a cup of dry filler or a lightweight bowl to a “kitchen” basket—playful delivery, not racing pressure.
activities.materials:
Large measuring cups
Lightweight filler or beanbags
Start/finish markers
Kitchen basket
Optional aprons
activities.preparation: Clear path. Mark start/kitchen. Practice walking feet.
activities.setup: Short straight path indoors or outdoors.
activities.steps:
1. Scoop or place item in cup.
2. Walk to kitchen basket.
3. Dump gently.
4. Walk back.
5. Cheer each delivery.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Walking feet, chef!
Carry careful.
To the kitchen!
Dump—thank you!
Your turn!
activities.observationOpportunities: Balance while carrying, waiting for turns, path following.
activities.safetyNotes: No running. Soft floors clear of toys. Lightweight loads only.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect cups; sweep filler.
teacherTips: Call it a delivery walk, not a race.
One child moving at a time if crowded.

substitutions.use: Carry empty pie pan or plastic apple

activities.adaptations: Push a cart/wagon; shorter path; hand-in-hand walk.
activities.extensions: Two-step delivery: wash station then kitchen.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger carry a stuffed apple; older scoop and deliver.
observationPrompts: Did the child carry without dumping early?
How did they wait?

activities.title: Little Apple Chef Parade
activities.objective: Close the week with a joyful chef parade that celebrates kitchen helpers and review words.
activities.description: Toddlers wear hats/aprons, carry a favorite kitchen prop, and parade to a simple chant before a group cheer.
activities.materials:
Chef hats/aprons
Props: spoons, pans, plastic apples
Parade path markers
Song/chant
Optional stickers
activities.preparation: Clear parade loop. Stage props basket.
activities.setup: Line-up spots; music ready.
activities.steps:
1. Choose a prop.
2. Parade slowly around the loop.
3. Freeze and show prop.
4. Name one kitchen word together.
5. Cheer “Little apple chefs!” + sticker optional.
activities.teacherLanguage:
Chefs in a line!
What are you carrying?
Stir? Pour? Mash?
Hooray apple chefs!
activities.observationOpportunities: Pride, recall of props/words, group participation comfort.
activities.safetyNotes: Walking feet. Props large and soft-edged. No forced speaking.
activities.cleanupTips: Collect props and hats.
teacherTips: Keep parade one or two loops only.

substitutions.use: Aprons or sticker badges

activities.adaptations: Wagon riders parade; nonverbal prop show; adult partner.
activities.extensions: Family photo opportunity if permitted.
activities.mixedAgeAdaptations: Infants watch and wave; toddlers parade.
observationPrompts: Did the child join the parade path?
Did they show a prop or word with support?
